note: Authored City Watch street cases, from docs/cases briefs CW-NC-01, CW-NC-08 and CW-NC-12. Original stories; unnamed witnesses are invented residents, not canon.

bridge.name: the Watch-side approach to Pon’s Bridge

quay.name: the quay by the Dock Warehouse

cases.title: The Bridge That Was Closed

partnerIntro.nobby: Nobby is good at blending into a crowd and noticing who pays whom.
partnerIntro.colon: Sergeant Colon is good at keeping people calm and in order, so you can work carefully.

cases.giverLine: Sergeant Colon: “Carters keep turning back from Pon’s Bridge. There’s a notice says it’s shut. The Watch never shut it, and nobody else is allowed to, so somebody’s having us on.”

giverLineByPartner.colon: Sergeant Colon: “Carters keep turning back from Pon’s Bridge. There’s a notice says it’s shut. The Watch never shut it, so I’m coming with you. Somebody’s having us on, and I don’t like being had on.”

cases.brief: Someone is diverting carts with a fake Watch notice. You have two leads, and you can take them in either order.

clues.notice: The notice at Pon’s Bridge says BRIDGE CLOSED, BY ORDER OF THE WATCH. It has no Watch stamp, no number and no signature. It is not a real Watch notice.
clues.tally: The quay clerk’s tally shows one fish trader arriving early on every morning the carts were sent round. He gains when everyone else is late.
clues.sighting: The quay clerk saw a man in a paint-spattered apron at the bridge at dawn, the morning the notice first went up.
clues.removed: You took the notice down. Pon’s Bridge is open to carts again.
clues.signmark: On the back of the notice, in small neat letters: ‘Pell & Daughter, Signs. Paid in advance.’ Someone ordered it from a sign-writer.
clues.apronman: A man in a paint-spattered apron came to straighten the notice, and the fish trader handed him coins.
clues.handover: Nobby saw the fish trader pay the man who looks after the notice. Money changed hands, in front of a witness.
clues.poster: The sign-writer from Pell & Daughter put the notice up: the clerk’s dawn sighting matches who made or tended it.

scenes.label: Inspect the bridge notice
scenes.hint: Shows whether this is a real Watch notice, and what it is doing to the carts.
scenes.title: The notice on Pon’s Bridge
scenes.text: BRIDGE CLOSED. ALL CARTS BY THE LONG ROUTE. BY ORDER OF THE WATCH. It is painted in confident capitals. Behind it, the bridge is open and perfectly sound. A queue of carts waits in front of it, and the drivers are not happy.

textByPartner.nobby: BRIDGE CLOSED. ALL CARTS BY THE LONG ROUTE. BY ORDER OF THE WATCH. Nobby squints at it. “That’s never Watch writing. It’s spelled right.” Behind it the bridge is perfectly sound, and a queue of unhappy carters waits in front.
textByPartner.colon: BRIDGE CLOSED. ALL CARTS BY THE LONG ROUTE. BY ORDER OF THE WATCH. Colon reads it twice, moving his lips. “No stamp, no number. I’d know if we’d done this. I’d have been asked to stand next to it.” A queue of unhappy carters waits in front.

scenes.label: Speak to the quay clerk
scenes.hint: Shows who gains when the carts are late, and who was seen at the bridge.
scenes.title: The quay clerk
scenes.speaker: The quay clerk
scenes.text: “I log every cart in. Mornings the bridge was ‘shut’, everyone came round the long way and arrived late. All except one fish trader, here early every time, selling to everybody else’s customers. Oh, and the first morning, there was a fellow at the bridge at dawn. Apron covered in paint.”

scenes.label: Decide what to do about the notice
scenes.hint: Take the notice down now, or leave it up a little longer to see who comes.
scenes.title: Take it down, or wait?
scenes.speaker: A carter at the front of the queue
scenes.text: “Are you taking that thing down or not? I’ve got a load of turnips that won’t get any fresher.”

choice.prompt: Decide what happens to the notice. You can’t do both.

options.label: Take the notice down now
options.tradeoff: The waiting carts cross straight away. Whoever set this up will probably stay away.

colon.text: Colon plants himself in front of the queue. “One at a time, gentlemen. There’s a bridge for everybody.” With the crowd calm, you lift the notice down carefully. On the back, in small neat letters: ‘Pell & Daughter, Signs. Paid in advance.’
colon.street: Pon’s Bridge is open again. The carts roll across while Sergeant Colon waves them through.

nobby.text: The moment the notice comes down, the drivers surge forward. It is trampled into the mud before you can look at it properly. Nobby holds up a muddy corner. “Well, it’s very closed now.”
nobby.street: Pon’s Bridge is open again. The carts rush across in a cheerful jam.

options.label: Leave it up a little longer and watch
options.tradeoff: The drivers keep waiting and grumbling. You might see who comes to check on the notice, or to pay for it.

nobby.text: Nobby slouches off into the queue and somehow looks exactly like a carter with a grievance. “Meet me back here at the notice,” he mutters.
nobby.street: The carts are still queuing at Pon’s Bridge. Nobby has vanished into the crowd.

colon.text: Colon nods and stands beside you, every inch a sergeant. “We’ll see who turns up,” he says. Nobody looks keen to turn up.
colon.street: The carts are still queuing at Pon’s Bridge, and the drivers are getting louder.

scenes.label: Keep watch on the notice
scenes.hint: See who comes to the notice while it is still up.
scenes.title: Watching the notice

textByPartner.nobby: A man in a paint-spattered apron strolls up to straighten the notice, very proud of his work. The early fish trader sidles over and presses a handful of coins into his hand. In the queue, Nobby catches your eye and taps his nose. Then you take the notice down, and the drivers who waited finally cross.
textByPartner.colon: A man in a paint-spattered apron turns into the street, sees Sergeant Colon’s uniform, and turns straight round again. The drivers have waited for nothing. With Colon keeping them in line, you lift the notice down carefully. On the back, in small neat letters: ‘Pell & Daughter, Signs. Paid in advance.’

streetByPartner.nobby: The drivers waited, but they cross Pon’s Bridge now. Nobby is grinning.
streetByPartner.colon: The drivers grumble as they finally cross Pon’s Bridge. Whoever was coming has gone.

file.label: Report to Captain Carrot
file.hint: File what you can prove. An honest partial report counts.
file.title: Reporting the closed bridge
file.prompt: “What did you establish at Pon’s Bridge?”
file.reject: Captain Carrot reads your notes twice. “I believe you believe it. But your evidence doesn’t show that yet.”

findings.label: The carters closed it themselves
findings.reject: “The carters were the ones losing money,” says Carrot. “Nothing you found points at them.”

findings.label: We reopened the route: the notice was fake and it’s down

replies.takedown: “Carts moving again and nobody hurt,” says Carrot. “That’s a good morning’s work. We don’t know who’s behind it yet, and you didn’t pretend to. That matters.”
replies.wait: “You held off to see who’d come, and it didn’t pay off this time,” says Carrot. “That happens. The route is open, and your report is honest.”

findings.reply: “The route is open again,” says Carrot. “Good, honest work.”

findings.label: We identified who posted the notice
findings.summary: Route reopened; the sign-writer who posted it identified.

replies.colon: “Pell & Daughter, Signs, and the clerk saw their man at dawn,” says Carrot. “So somebody ordered this notice. That’s our next question for Pell. Well worked, both of you.”
replies.nobby: “The man in the apron, and the clerk saw him at dawn,” says Carrot. “That’s who put it up. Who he did it for is another matter.”

findings.reply: “That’s who put it up,” says Carrot.

findings.label: We proved who paid for it
findings.reject: “Being first to the quay isn’t paying for a notice,” says Carrot. “Did anyone actually see money change hands?”
findings.summary: Fish trader proved to have paid for the fake notice.
findings.reply: “Nobby saw the fish trader pay for it, and the clerk’s tally shows exactly why he would,” says Carrot. “The notice, the motive and the money. I’ll have a long word with our fish trader. With paperwork.”

cases.title: A Receipt for a Raincoat
cases.where: the Market and the Mended Drum
cases.giverLine: Sergeant Colon: “Gentleman says his raincoat’s on a stall by the Market Hall, and the stallholder’s got a receipt for it. Now, I’m not saying anyone’s lying. I’m saying someone’s wrong, and I’d like it to be someone who isn’t me.”
cases.brief: Find out whose coat it is, and how a receipt came to be with it. Get the coat home without accusing anyone you can’t prove did wrong.

clues.seam: The coat on the stall has a little anchor darned into the collar, exactly as the owner described. It is his coat.
clues.receipt: The stallholder’s receipt is genuine, from a pawnshop, but it describes a coat with brass buttons and a hood. This coat has horn buttons and no hood.
clues.mixup: At the Mended Drum, two coats hung on one peg. A customer took the wrong one home, then sold it with the receipt for his own coat. The stallholder bought it honestly.

scenes.label: Examine the raincoat
scenes.title: A raincoat on a stall
scenes.text: A sturdy oilskin raincoat, much loved and much mended. Inside the collar someone has darned a tiny anchor in thick thread, just as the owner said.

scenes.label: Read the stallholder’s receipt
scenes.title: The stallholder’s receipt
scenes.speaker: The stallholder
scenes.text: “Bought fair and square, I did. Here’s the receipt.” The receipt is real enough. It describes a raincoat with brass buttons and a hood. The coat in front of you has horn buttons and nowhere to keep a hood.

scenes.label: Decide how to handle the coat
scenes.title: The coat and the receipt
scenes.speaker: The stallholder
scenes.text: “If it’s his coat, it’s his coat. But I paid for it, and I don’t like being called a thief.”

choice.prompt: You can settle this now, or dig into how the wrong receipt got here.

options.label: Arrange the return now, no accusations
options.text: You agree the coat goes home, and promise the stallholder the receipt question will be looked into. Nobody is called a thief. Everybody is slightly damp.

options.label: Find out how the wrong receipt got here
options.text: The stallholder remembers where it came from: “Bloke from the Mended Drum sold it me. Said he had the receipt to prove it was his.”

scenes.label: Ask about the coat at the Mended Drum
scenes.title: Coats at the Mended Drum
scenes.speaker: A regular by the door
scenes.text: “Peg by the door only takes one coat, so people hang two. Last wet night, two raincoats, one peg. Fellow grabbed the wrong one going home, sold it the next day with his own receipt, thinking it was his. Came back this morning looking for his real one, very embarrassed.”

file.label: Report to Sergeant Colon
file.title: Reporting the raincoat
file.prompt: “Right then. Whose coat is it, and is anybody going in the cells?”
file.reject: Colon squints at your notes. “That’s not what this says, is it? Have another look.”

findings.label: The stallholder stole the coat
findings.reject: “The stallholder paid for it and kept the receipt,” says Colon. “That’s not theft. That’s bad luck with paperwork.”

findings.label: It’s the owner’s coat: returned, nobody blamed
findings.summary: Coat returned; how the receipt got there was left open.
findings.reply: “Coat goes home, nobody gets accused of anything they didn’t do,” says Colon. “Proper policing, that. The receipt business can stay a mystery. The city’s full of them.”

findings.label: An honest mix-up at the Mended Drum: wrong coat, wrong receipt
findings.summary: Honest mix-up explained; coat returned, nobody to blame.
findings.reply: “Two coats, one peg,” says Colon, delighted. “Nobody’s a criminal, everybody gets their own coat back, and I get to write ‘peg-related’ on a form. Best kind of case.”

cases.title: The Fine on the Nail
cases.giverLine: Sergeant Colon: “People in the Shades are finding fines nailed to their doors. Watch fines, supposedly. Thing is, we don’t do fines by nail. We don’t hardly do fines at all, it’s all the writing.”
cases.brief: Check whether the fines are real, find out if anyone has actually paid, and stop people being cheated. You never pay anything yourself.

clues.notice: The notice nailed in the Shades says ‘FINE: 3 coins for Unlicensed Washing. Pay the collector. By order of the Watch.’ No signature, no number.
clues.norecord: The duty desk has no fines for washing, no collector, and no record of any notices in the Shades. The Watch never issued them.
clues.paid: A neighbour paid 3 coins to a man in a long coat who said he was collecting for the Watch. Money was really taken.
clues.collector: You watched the collector make his rounds and saw him take another payment. You can describe him and where he goes.

scenes.label: Read the notice on the nail
scenes.title: A fine on a nail
scenes.text: FINE: 3 COINS FOR UNLICENSED WASHING. PAY THE COLLECTOR. BY ORDER OF THE WATCH. It is nailed to a door that has clearly not been washed, licensed or otherwise, in years.

scenes.label: Check the duty desk records
scenes.title: The duty desk
scenes.speaker: The desk officer
scenes.text: “Fines for washing? In the Shades? We’d be more likely to give out medals for it.” The ledger has no such fine, no collector, and nothing about the Shades but the usual.

scenes.label: Decide what to tell the residents
scenes.title: Warn them, or watch first?
scenes.speaker: A resident
scenes.text: “So it’s not real? Then who’s been coming round for the money?”

choice.prompt: Warning everyone now stops anyone else paying. Keeping quiet a little longer might show you who is collecting.

options.label: Warn the street now: nobody pays
options.text: Word travels down the street faster than you can walk it. Nobody else will be paying any fines today. Somebody mentions a neighbour by the Market who already paid.

options.label: Say nothing yet and watch for the collector
options.text: You ask the resident to keep this between you for an hour. They agree, with the expression of someone who will tell everyone in an hour and five minutes. The collector works the Market side next, they say.

scenes.label: Talk to the neighbour who paid
scenes.title: The neighbour who paid
scenes.speaker: A neighbour
scenes.text: “Three coins, I gave him. Long coat, very polite, said it was for the Watch. I thought, well, at least it’s not for the Thieves’ Guild. Should I have thought harder?”

scenes.label: Watch the collector make his rounds
scenes.title: Watching the collector
scenes.text: A man in a long coat works along the Market side, tapping each notice and holding out his hand. A woman pays him three coins. You note his face, his coat and where he goes next. Then you warn the street, so nobody else pays.

file.label: Report to Captain Carrot
file.title: Reporting the fines
file.prompt: “Are these fines real? And if not, has anybody been cheated?”
file.reject: Carrot shakes his head gently. “Your notes don’t say that yet. What do you actually know?”

findings.label: The fines are real, so residents should pay
findings.reject: “No signature, no record at the desk,” says Carrot. “The Watch doesn’t fine people by nail.”

findings.label: False notices: no such fine exists
findings.summary: Notices shown to be fake; no one proven to have been cheated.
findings.reply: “Good,” says Carrot. “Fake notices are a nuisance, and you’ve shown they’re fake. If anyone was actually paid, we’ll need a witness to prove it.”

findings.label: Fraud: money was taken for a fake fine
findings.summary: Fraud proven: money was taken for fake fines.

replies.warn: “You warned them first and still found the proof,” says Carrot. “Nobody else paid today because of you. We don’t know the collector’s face yet, but we know what he did.”

findings.reply: “The notice was fake and somebody paid,” says Carrot. “That’s fraud, and it’s proven.”

findings.label: Fraud by the collector you watched
findings.summary: Collector seen taking money; fraud proven and he can be found.
findings.reply: “Fake fine, a payment you saw, and a description good enough to find him,” says Carrot. “And you warned the street once you had it. That’s the job done properly.”
